Verdict

No confirmed indicators of a malicious supply-chain compromise were found. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard hatchling.build backend. In the provided content, there is no evidence of install-time custom build hooks, setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, or usercustomize.py.
  • [project.scripts] clem2itunes = "clem2itunes.main:main" is a normal console_scripts entry point and requires the user to run the command. This is not evidence of malicious automatic execution.
  • clem2itunes/__main__.py calls main() only for python -m clem2itunes, which is user-triggered. It is not an install-time or interpreter-startup execution path.
  • clem2itunes/__init__.py only imports create_library and defines the version; no suspicious import-time side effects were identified.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential harvesting: No evidence was found of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallets, kubeconfigs, or similar secrets.
  • Exfiltration/networking: URLs in README/PKG-INFO, such as GitHub, ReadTheDocs, and shields.io, appear to be documentation/badge links. No code evidence of attacker-controlled C2 or upload endpoints was identified.
  • Staging/archiving: No evidence was found of collecting files into tar/zip/base64 archives or temporary staging for upload.
  • Persistence: No evidence was found of systemd units, cron jobs, shell profile modification, LaunchAgents, or self-reinstall loops. .gitignore entries such as /.bashrc and /.zshrc are ignore patterns only, not code that modifies or creates those files.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence was found of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection behavior.
  • Obfuscation/loaders: The subprocess wrapper and regex usage appear consistent with the package’s audio/sync functionality. No evidence was found of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal loaders, downloader stubs, or malicious staged loading.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The dependencies in pyproject.toml appear broadly consistent with the project description and do not show clear evidence of token-theft dependency insertion.
  • The sdist include configuration explicitly lists clem2itunes, man, and tests. In the provided file list, no unexplained native binaries, hidden executable payloads, .dist-info manipulation, or typosquatting indicators were identified.
  • Including .gitignore may be unnecessary for distribution quality, but it is not by itself malicious supply-chain evidence.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input corpus includes only a subset of the 17 extracted files. In particular, clem2itunes/index.js is invoked by the sync command through osascript -l JavaScript, but its contents were not provided, so that file should be reviewed.
  • If a wheel artifact exists separately, compare it against the sdist for file or behavior mismatches.
